hook_text: 16 trays of 25 rolls. Do not multiply. Push the trays together and the answer falls out.
clip_script: Bakery in Kroonstad, 16 trays, 25 rolls each. 16 times 25 looks hard. Push the trays together in pairs: 8 trays of 50. Same rolls, friendlier numbers. Push again: 4 trays of 100. Four hundred rolls. That is doubling and halving. Halve one number, double the other, the answer never changes. Now the chairs: 48 times 5. Round up: 50 times 5 is 250, take off the extra two fives, 10, so 240. Now check with the opposite operation. 240 divided by 5. Two hundred divided by 5 is 40, forty divided by 5 is 8. 48. It undoes perfectly. Estimate, make the numbers friendly, then divide to prove it. Two techniques on every sum, and nothing slips through.
visual_style: Whiteboard trays sliding together in pairs with the roll count unchanged; a 48 bending up to 50 with a minus 10 tag; a division arrow looping back to the start.
mood: Hands-on and satisfying, like tidying a bakery.
pacing: Trays pushed together twice, the compensation trick, then the division check and the rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find a multiplication in your kitchen you can halve and double.
